# Tobit Chapter 6 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 6 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_006_page_001.jpg

---

**1** They set out together — the dog running ahead — and spent their first night camped beside the Tigris.

**2** When Tobias waded in at the bank to wash his feet, a great fish lunged out of the water and snapped at his foot. He shouted in terror.

**3** "Grab it!" the angel said. Tobias seized the fish and wrestled it up onto the bank.

**4** "Now gut it," said the angel. "Take out the heart, the liver, and the gall, and keep them safe."

**5** Tobias did as he was told. He cut the fish open, took out the organs, and set them aside. He grilled part of the fish and ate his fill; the rest he packed in salt for the journey.

The two of them walked on, and by degrees the landscape of Media began to open before them.

**6** After a while, Tobias turned to his companion. "Azariah — what exactly are these fish organs good for? Why would someone use a fish's heart and liver and gall as medicine?"

**7** "Here's what they're for," Raphael said. "If someone is tormented by a demon or an evil spirit, you burn the heart and liver as smoke before them — and the person is freed from that torment, permanently.

**8** The gall you smear on someone's eyes where they've gone white — and it heals them."

**9** As they neared Media and came into the approaches of Ecbatana,

**10** Raphael spoke. "Tobias." "Yes?" "Tonight we're going to stay with a man named Raguel. He's a relative of yours. He has one daughter — her name is Sarah.

**11** She's his only child — no sons, no other daughters. Everything he owns will pass to you as his nearest heir. The girl herself is sensible and brave and very beautiful, and her father is a good man.

**12** You have every right to marry her. Trust me on this — tonight I'll talk to her father, and we'll arrange for you to take her as your bride. When we come back from Rages, we can hold the wedding. I know Raguel can't turn you down or give her to someone else — the law of Moses would bring a sentence of death on him for that. You're her rightful heir. So let me speak to her father tonight, and we'll arrange the betrothal."

**13** "Brother Azariah," Tobias said, "I've already heard what happened. Seven men have married that girl. Every single one of them died in the bridal chamber on the very night of the wedding. There's a demon, they say — a demon that kills them.

**14** I'm scared. It doesn't hurt Sarah — it just kills every man who tries to be with her. I'm an only child. If I die, it will kill my parents too — they'll die of grief, and there'll be no one left to bury them."

**15** "Have you forgotten what your father told you?" Raphael said. "He commanded you to marry from your own family. Don't let this demon frighten you. Take her.

**16** I'm telling you: tonight, she will be yours.

**17** When you go into the bridal chamber, take the heart and liver from what we saved and burn them on the incense coals. The smoke will fill the room,

**18** and when the demon smells it, he'll run — and he'll never come back. Then, before you come together, both of you get up and pray. Ask the Lord of heaven to protect you and show you mercy. Don't be afraid. She was made for you before the beginning of time. You will rescue her, and she will come with you, and I believe you'll have a family together. Don't be troubled."

As Tobias listened to every word Raphael said — and understood that Sarah was his own flesh and blood, his father's kin — something happened inside him. He fell in love with her. His heart held fast to her, and would not let go.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **v. 2 — "snapped at his foot"**: Greek *katapein ton poda* (tried to swallow the foot). A large Tigris catfish lunging at a washing foot is plausible. PNEUMA renders it with physical immediacy.
- **v. 7 — "permanently"**: Greek *eti ouketi* (no more, ever again). The demonic release is total and permanent. PNEUMA makes this explicit since modern readers may miss the Greek double negative.
- **v. 8 — "where they've gone white"**: Greek *leukōmata* — corneal deposits/films causing blindness. The reader knows from ch. 2 that this is exactly Tobit's condition. PNEUMA renders it as visual description rather than medical term.
- **v. 12 — "the law of Moses would bring a sentence of death"**: PNEUMA makes the legal consequence clear in plain terms. The levirate principle is not footnoted but dramatized.
- **vv. 13–14 — Tobias's fear**: This is genuine, understandable human fear. PNEUMA preserves it without softening. Seven dead husbands is terrifying information. The fear makes Tobias real, not cowardly.
- **v. 18 — "before the beginning of time"**: *Ap' aiōnos* (from eternity). PNEUMA renders this as "before the beginning of time" — an accessible phrase for the predestination concept.
- **Final verse**: "His heart held fast to her, and would not let go" — PNEUMA expands the Genesis echo (*proskollān*) into a full emotional clause rather than a single verb. The falling-in-love moment is the chapter's emotional climax and deserves its own weight. — PNEUMA
